result.title: SKILL.PNG: Learning Agent Skills in Pixel Space
result.summary: AI agents are commonly specialized for new tasks and domains using skills, i.e. natural language instructions placed in their context. However, the discrete nature of textual skills prevents continuous optimization. Gradient-based approaches such as finetuning, on the other hand, are typically model-specific, preventing skill transfer across different agents. Since many agents today are built on vision-language models (VLMs), we can address these limitations by introducing Skill.png: a method for obtaining skill-like image inputs whose pixels are optimized with gradient descent through the vision encoder of a frozen VLM. Image skills are compatible with any VLM, and a single image can be optimized jointly for an ensemble of models. We show that Skill.png significantly outperforms state-of-the-art textual skills optimized using frontier LLMs in 9 of 16 settings (across 4 VLMs and 4 benchmarks) while requiring only 64 to 256 image tokens instead of roughly 900 to 2000 text tokens at inference time. Hybrid skills, i.e. text and image skills jointly optimized, further improve agent performance. Moreover, an image optimized with an ensemble of VLMs can successfully transfer across the models in the ensemble. Skill.png thus presents the first agent skill that can be optimized with gradient descent while retaining transfer benefits of text skills. Our code is available at: https://github.com/omseeth/skill.png

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Skill.png：把 agent skill 表示成图像，像素经由冻结 VLM 的视觉编码器做梯度优化，单张图可针对多模型集成联合优化；在 4 个 VLM、4 个基准的 16 个设置中 9 个优于前沿 LLM 优化的文本 skill，且推理时仅需 64–256 个图像 token，文本 skill 约需 900–2000 个，文本+图像混合 skill 进一步提升表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作显示视觉通道可承载并压缩指令类信息、且梯度能穿过冻结视觉编码器，可供核查「视觉旁路」与视觉 token 实际被使用程度的问题，但它优化的是技能条件而非 latent 推理状态，迁移价值需进一步确认。
